explanation:
Safety verdict: BLOCK an unprotected 18.10.0 migration; retain and rebase 0090, family-usage-pipeline and 0048, and do not describe 0090 as an exactly-once refresh guarantee. The inspected upstream changes do not replace these protections; the findings distinguish losses relative to replay-18.7.0 from a current-baseline provider-filter defect, while the residual crash/ambiguous-exchange risks below already exist in both baselines rather than being new upstream regressions.

Comparison roots: P=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/pristine-18.7.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi; B=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/replay-18.7.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi; T=/tmp/omp-18100-audit-cd9kqmcj/pristine-18.10.0/node_modules/@oh-my-pi. Only static source/patch inspection was performed; no credentials, production databases, network probes, builds or tests were used. Partial replay-18.10.0 was not used as a candidate.

REDEMPTION MAP. T/pi-ai/src/auth/select.ts:731-776 sends eager selection and forced auth recovery to OAuthRefresher.refresh; final selection does the same at :1063-1087. T/pi-ai/src/auth/usage.ts:222-249 proactively refreshes near-expiry credentials through that refresher. T/pi-ai/src/auth/oauth.ts:366-375 exposes refreshById and refreshStored; broker scheduler T/pi-ai/src/auth-broker/refresher.ts:112 and POST handler server.ts:933-941 call oauth.refresh. Gateway dispatch.ts:219-225 sends forceRefresh and auth-recovery through selection, not a separate provider exchange. Remote-store.ts:1233-1241 delegates by id, client.ts:322-330 transports reason, and server.ts:935-940 consumes it explicitly. Broker CLI auth-broker-cli.ts:130-136 installs the local-mint override; :127 calls the generic registry refresh. The registry engine refresh.ts:74-98 posts the refresh grant and runs after-refresh hooks; the Anthropic rule is pi-catalog/src/compat/rules/auth/anthropic.kdl:37-53. The public registry refreshOAuthToken API can also redeem directly; no additional internal Anthropic caller outside the mapped local/override paths was found. Missing credential ids bypass both the per-id singleflight and durable lease in auth/refresh.ts:459-460,489,544; usage obtains that id by matching current pool entries (pool.ts:796-816), so stale/removed usage descriptors are not intrinsically protected. This latter residual route predates the target changes and deserves a focused follow-up, not a new-upstream finding.

OWNERSHIP AND RESIDUAL SAFETY. Singleflight maps in refresh.ts:100-101 are per OAuthRefresher instance and row id, not globally process-wide; refreshById converges onto the refresh singleflight, and separate SQLite-backed instances rely on the lease. Lease acquisition is atomic per credential row, renewals run every 5s, TTL is 15s, and the normal operation timeout is 10s. T/sqlite-credential-store.ts:472-482 fences CAS by row bytes, owner and expiry; :543-551 permits takeover after expiry, while :555-559 renews only the same owner. Normal concurrent expired-token refreshes therefore reload the durable winner rather than both exchanging. Forced refresh intentionally omits observedCredential (refresh.ts:490-493), so distinct-process force calls may serially mint successive tokens; that is token churn, not necessarily duplicate redemption of the same token. A renewal failure prevents persistence, and the local pre-CAS renewal repairs timer starvation only while ownership has not actually changed.

0090 DOES NOT CLOSE THE AMBIGUOUS-EXCHANGE WINDOW. A crash after the provider consumes R0 but before R1 is durably written leaves R0 on disk; the lease is later stealable and a future request can redeem R0 again. A thrown CAS write has the same lost-result consequence: tryUpdateAuthCredentialIfMatches propagates the write error (:1507-1553), refreshStored releases its lease in finally (:363-366), and there is no durable attempt/uncertain marker or retained response. An owner timeout still races away from the provider promise (:577-593); the generic engine also checks cancellation after receiving the token response (registry/engine/refresh.ts:87). A paused process can lose a lease while its exchange remains outstanding, and the new owner can post the same stored refresh token; fencing protects the database winner, not the provider's external side effect. These are CURRENT-BASELINE and TARGET residual risks, not introduced regressions, and 0090 is necessary but insufficient for a strict no-duplicate-redemption claim. Minimal stronger requirement, if strict safety is mandatory: durably record an attempt before redemption, distinguish unstarted from ambiguous/consumed states, prohibit blind takeover/re-redemption of an unresolved attempt, and provide explicit reauthentication/reconciliation instead of retrying the old token; without provider idempotency/recovery support, safety requires sacrificing automatic availability in the crash window. Provider behavior and any recovery endpoint remain unverified.

INVALID_GRANT AND REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES. Definitive failure is CAS-disabled with owner fencing inside refreshStored (:280-310); outer disableDefinitiveFailure (:384-425) checks whether a peer's refresh token changed before disabling. Do not report unconditional peer deletion: these guards exist. Do not report every replaceById as an unconditional write: pool.ts:476-503 performs CAS and reloads a winning peer. It still does not justify reconstructing a stale row after the owner path, because the CAS expected value comes from the current in-memory pool, not the original refresh observation. Do not report getOAuthApiKey as a second mint: registry/oauth/index.ts:126 onward explicitly requires an already-fresh credential. The new refreshOAuthCredentialMints flag is consumed by auth-storage.ts:195 and refresh.ts:141-145,351,470, with matching published declarations; broker creation explicitly sets it. That is a useful upstream cooldown repair, not replacement of 0090. Broker CLI :127 omits the provider signal, but that omission already exists in pristine18.7; it must not be mislabeled a new18.10 regression. Broker client fetchRaw retries transport failures for POST as well as GET (:473-515); a repeated forced request can mint again after a lost broker response, while auth-recovery reuse reduces churn only after a remembered successful local mint. No claim of provider-side token revocation semantics was experimentally verified.

FAMILY DISPOSITIONS AND MIGRATION REQUIREMENTS. 0090-oauth-durable-refresh: RETAIN/REBASE; BLOCK retirement. Preserve waiter-only cancellation after lease acquisition, pre-CAS same-owner renewal, owner-only persistence in refresh/select/usage, and login-only Anthropic bootstrap enrichment; carry the anthropic.d.ts documentation update. Merge with the upstream overrideMints and reason-forwarding changes rather than reverting them. Acceptance: a cancelled initiating waiter must not cancel the shared owner, the refreshed row must be persisted once before later resolution, and delayed bootstrap must never sit between Anthropic exchange and durable commit. family-usage-pipeline: RETAIN/REBASE with a same-family repair for broker filtering. Preserve canonical Anthropic endpoint cache keys and read-only legacy-key adoption, fresh/last-good lookup, active-provider fan-out, statusline turn/repaint gates and Ollama Cloud session/weekly usage mapping. T/usage-cache.ts:223-224,280-295 still keys raw URLs, so no equivalence supports retirement. Update pi-ai UsageApi/UsageService/UsageCache source and declarations, coding-agent AgentSession source/declaration and status-line-host, and pi-tui host source/declaration/component together; include broker request/store/client/server options if the filter is promised across remote storage. 0048-advisor-quota-rotation-bound: RETAIN/REBASE. Target session-advisors.ts:2122 still returns on every successful same-provider quota rotation before checking fallback. Preserve one-grace accounting and success reset, incorporating the upstream account-policy branch without conflating account-policy denial with quota exhaustion; acceptance is that a second consecutive same-provider quota rotation proceeds to the configured cross-provider fallback and a successful turn restores the grace. This family changes private state, not a public declaration surface.

DATABASE AND ROLLBACK. The pristine18.7-to18.10 sqlite-credential-store diff introduces block-scope/batch readers and throttled expiry sweeps, not a new credential/lease/revision schema. Existing auth change revision and local revision accounting remain at T:2040-2092; identical CAS writes avoid revision churn at :1518-1527. The lease table is already present in P and is unchanged by 0090; client_usage.app migration is pre-existing rather than a new18.10 rollback blocker. Family usage cache adoption is additive and preserves old keys and expiry, not a destructive SQL migration. For these owned families, no new schema-based prohibition on code rollback was found, but rollback must preserve the CURRENT credential DB and its rotated token bytes: restoring a pre-upgrade DB snapshot can restore already-consumed refresh tokens even when schemas match. Do not operate old unprotected and patched refresh owners concurrently and call that safe rollback. The full application's other DB migrations are outside this ownership slice.

HIGH-VALUE SYNTHETIC PROBES FOR THE PARENT (not executed). (1) Actual AuthStorage plus two real private SQLite connections and a gated synthetic refresh override: abort the first caller after redemption begins, retain a second waiter, resolve R1, and assert one exchange, one durable winner and no R0 reuse; add a same-process pool reload between owner completion and selection continuation to catch stale caller re-persistence. Compare B and T; this discriminates the central 0090 loss without any provider requests. (2) Same fixture with one successful exchange followed by a failing fenced write, and separately an expired/stolen lease: inspect the next request's token and demonstrate the residual ambiguity rather than asserting exactly-once behavior from the presence of CAS. A kill-after-redemption child process is useful only if the simpler write-failure case does not settle the acceptance decision. (3) Invoke the real UsageService.reports({providers:[nonAnthropic]}) once with a local store and once with a synthetic broker transport backed by real routing; count per-provider usage invocations and assert Anthropic is untouched. This distinguishes the baseline filter gap and validates the entire new option consumer chain. Advisor acceptance can be exercised with two consecutive real recovery calls and a success reset if that family is rebased; no broad suite expansion is proposed.

Remaining uncertainties: actual provider token-reuse/revocation semantics, power-loss durability under SQLite synchronous=NORMAL, timing-dependent failure frequency, and strict exactly-once recovery feasibility are not established by source inspection. No genuine new18.10 duplicate-redemption bug independent of the lost local protection was proven in this slice. All three required policy grep checks were performed successfully at delivery.

findings.title: Retain waiter-only cancellation when rebasing the durable refresh owner
findings.body: MIGRATION LOSS, not a new pristine-upstream regression: compared with patched18.7, target18.10 again combines the initiating caller's signal with the owner signal before invoking the token exchange. Selection, usage timeout and broker request-disconnect callers all reach this path. If that caller aborts after Anthropic accepts R0, Promise.race in #requestOAuthCredentialRefresh rejects, refreshStored releases the lease without saving R1, and a subsequent request can redeem the persisted R0 again. Restore 0090's separation between cancellation of a caller's wait and the bounded provider-to-store owner operation; retain the upstream reason forwarding and overrideMints behavior.

findings.title: Keep Anthropic bootstrap enrichment out of refresh completion
findings.body: MIGRATION LOSS: target18.10 restores bootstrap fetching when the refresh response lacks accountId or email, whereas 0090 preserves stored identity and returns immediately in the refresh phase. The generic exchange engine awaits this hook after the refresh grant has succeeded; bootstrap has a 30-second timeout while OAuthRefresher abandons the refresh promise after 10 seconds. A slow bootstrap therefore discards newly rotated credentials before persistence and leaves the already-redeemed refresh token stored. Retain the login-only bootstrap branch and matching declaration documentation; test a synthetic successful token response with omitted identity and a deliberately unresolved bootstrap fetch.

findings.title: Preserve owner-only persistence after a lease-backed refresh
findings.body: MIGRATION LOSS: target18.10 restores caller-side merging/persistence in selection after refreshStored already saved or reloaded the winning row; equivalent removed 0090 guards also affect usage.ts:188-209 and refreshById at refresh.ts:675-682. For example, when a peer changes non-token credential metadata before the owner reads its row, the owner correctly preserves that newer metadata, but selection merges returned token fields into its pre-await credential and replaceById compares against the now-current pool, allowing stale metadata to overwrite the owner winner. A same-process pool reload between completion and continuation can likewise let stale token bytes be compared against a newer pool row. Restore the lease-backed resync/read-only return branches in all three callers; preserve the existing CAS for stores without leases rather than treating it as a substitute for owner-only persistence.

findings.title: Renew the same refresh owner immediately before the fenced commit
findings.body: MIGRATION LOSS: the patched baseline renews the same owner before persistence, but target18.10 proceeds directly from the completed exchange to the expiry-fenced CAS. If event-loop starvation expires the lease after successful redemption and no peer has taken over, the target rejects its own commit and reloads the old row, losing the newly rotated token. Restore 0090's immediate same-owner renewal before CAS; do not weaken the owner or row-byte fence, since an actual takeover must still win. This repairs the no-takeover starvation case only and must not be presented as solving crash-after-redemption or overlapping external exchanges.

findings.title: Forward the usage provider filter through the broker branch
findings.body: CURRENT-BASELINE FAMILY DEFECT: family-usage-pipeline adds providers to reports and passes the active provider from the statusline, but applies it only at the final local branch. With a RemoteAuthCredentialStore, reports enters storeOverride first, calls it without options and returns broker-wide reports; the broker server in turn invokes storage.usage.reports without a provider filter. Consequently a non-Anthropic session's new repaint/turn polling still fetches Anthropic usage whenever the broker cache expires, contrary to the filter contract and the family's per-provider rate-limit protection. Propagate a normalized provider filter through the store hook, broker client/query, server and in-flight/cache identity, and intersect runtime-local fallback providers with that filter; filtering the returned array alone does not prevent the unwanted provider request.

findings.title: Retain the advisor quota-rotation grace before provider fallback
findings.body: MIGRATION LOSS: stock18.10 again returns true immediately for every successful same-provider quota rotation. With at least three accounts and repeated quota failures, recovery uses another account instead of reaching the configured cross-provider fallback after the single grace rotation implemented by 0048; the retry settings and fallback chain are checked only below this return. Rebase the per-advisor provider/count state and success reset onto the target recovery method, preserving the new account-policy handling separately. Validate a second consecutive switched quota outcome against an available fallback, then a successful turn followed by a new quota episode.
